title.narrative: Madagascar Second Equitable and Resilient Growth Development Policy Operation

description.narrative: The Program Development Objectives are to: (i) Strengthen fiscal management; and (ii) Improve the business environment, with a focus on telecoms, energy, and mining.

The development objectives of Second Equitable and Resilient Growth Development Policy Operation Project for Madagascar are to: (i) Strengthen fiscal management; and (ii) Improve the business environment, with a focus on telecoms, energy, and mining. The Government of Madagascar's reform program is anchored in the Strategic Development Plan for Madagascar (PEM) and the General State Policy (PGE). The PEM, the country's vision for 2040, aims to address long-standing development issues and close the development gap through 13 commitments articulated around three key pillars: social (human development, jobs, equality/gender, sport and culture), growth (energy and water, industrialization, agriculture and food security, modernization), and environment (sustainable natural resource management) and governance as a cross-cutting theme. It targets increased public and private investments and seeks to mitigate climate risks. The key reform areas supported by the Development Policy Operation (DPO) are consistent with the CPF (FY23-27) and draw on lessons from the previous CPF (FY18-22). The DPO complements other World Bank-financed operations and is anchored in recent analytical studies and technical assistance programs. The operation supports several outcome areas of the new corporate score card. The operation supports Maximizing Finance for Development (MFD) and Private Capital Enabling (PCE) reforms. The PAs are aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

title.narrative: RI#1. Share of investment projects in the budget that have been prioritized following the public investment project (PIP) selection criteria including ratings on climate resilient risk

comment.narrative: The public investment management (PIM) manual has been introduced and the selection process defined in the manual has been applied in a partial basis. The PIP selection committee is not yet operational during the project selection process of the 2026 draft budget law preparation. The committee is expected to be in place for the 2027 budget preparation cycle. The PIP database is not yet available. The RI will be assessed in the process of the 2027 draft budget law preparation

title.narrative: RI#5. Share of the FNP funds allocated to the communes by the end of the first semester of each year according to the new framework

comment.narrative: Progress is delayed. The transfers were execuced with delays in 2023. The transfers planned in 2024 and 2025 remain pending. The list of beneficiaries (communes) is ready. The delays have been driven in part by slower-than-expected recruitment of engineering firms to support communes in the infrastructures construction (assistance to contracting authority).

title.narrative: RI#4. Communes receiving transfers from the Treasury through an e-wallet in Treasury Single Platform (PUT)

comment.narrative: Implementation is progressing. The roll-out of e-wallet for communes is advancing. To accelerate the process, the Treasury launched an enrollment campaign in February 2026 and aims to reach 140 communes by May 2026. Continued scaling will be needed to reach the end-target (at least 200).

title.narrative: RI#10. JIRAMA's annual earnings before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA) before transfers from the central government (billion of ariary)

comment.narrative: EBITDA improved relative to the baseline but remains negative. It reflects the need for contined efforts to improves JIRAMA's operational and financial performance through the implementation of its Recovery Plan. The plan includes measures to strengthen JIRAMA's governance, reduce operational losses, and shift energy generation toward renewable sources to reduce costs. Implementation of the debt restructuring plan targeting arrears owned to the private sector IPPs will be instrumental in unlocking additional renewable energy capacity

title.narrative: RI#13. Number of gold export companies approved by the Council of Ministers and volume of official gold exports

comment.narrative: Following the reopening of formal gold export, the government granted six licenses for "comptoirs de l'or" (gold trading houses), and the licenses expired in October 2024. The trading houses got extension for export after license expiration to enable them to process their stock of gold. However, limited formal export (0.013 ton in 2025) has been recorded with the licensed trading houses. The Central Bank launched a call for expression of interest has been launched in June 2025 to identify companies willing to supply gold to the Central Bank and to export gold. The new government is currently assessing candidates. Meanwhile, a gold sector recovery plan (Note sur le Plan de Relance du Secteur AurifEre) has been prepared. Timely clarification of the policy framework and operational steps will be critical to accelerate formal exports toward the target.

title.narrative: RI#11. Renewable energy made available to JIRAMA by private sector operators

comment.narrative: Since the 2023 reform, 11 MW of additional renewable energy capacity has been supplied by the private sector to JIRAMA. Further scale-up will depend on continued implementation of JIRAMA's recovery plan (particularly the implementation of the debt restructuring plan) to restore confidence and unlock additional private renewable supply.

title.narrative: RI#7. Conversion rate between prospects (lead) and investors

comment.narrative: Progress is close to the end target. The EDBM reported US$155 million of realized investments (converted) in 2024 from projects that benefited from its facilitation support. From January to August 2025, EBDM supported 86 investment projects with announced investments totally US$790 million (including 34 new projects), of which 21 projects valued at US$245 million have been realized.
